intro: SpaceX closes its record $60B all-stock acquisition of Cursor maker Anysphere, folding the coding tool into a new SpaceXAI division alongside Grok. GitHub ships Grok 4.6 in Copilot and adds token refresh for OAuth apps, while an unpatched GeoServer zero-day sees active exploitation. And in Bitcoin, Cboe files for the first US 3x-leveraged BTC/ETH ETFs as Trump prepares to meet crypto executives and regulators at the White House.

items.headline: SpaceX finalizes $60 billion acquisition of Cursor maker Anysphere
items.summary: SpaceX closed its all-stock purchase of Anysphere, the startup behind the widely used Cursor code editor, folding it into a new SpaceXAI division alongside xAI's Grok. It's the largest startup acquisition on record.
items.why: Consolidates one of the most popular AI coding tools inside SpaceX/xAI, reshaping the competitive map against Anthropic, OpenAI and Microsoft-backed rivals.

items.headline: Grok Bot goes live in Cursor as developers flag vendor lock-in
items.summary: Days after the deal closed, SpaceXAI's always-on 'Grok Bot' agents — which sign into a user's own apps and keep working in the background — rolled out to Cursor's paying tiers. Commentators note the acquisition leaves few independent, privacy-neutral AI coding tools above hobbyist scale.
items.why: Code written in Cursor now feeds a model stack owned by SpaceX — a real shift in who controls the data behind one of the most-used coding tools.

items.headline: Alibaba's Qwen releases open-weight Qwen3.8-27B under Apache 2.0
items.summary: The 27-billion-parameter multimodal dense model ships with a 262K native context window (extendable to 1M) and, per Qwen, beats the larger Qwen3.7-Plus on coding and office tasks while running on a single consumer GPU.
items.why: Another capable, permissively licensed open-weight model keeps pricing pressure on proprietary labs, extending a strong run of releases from Chinese labs this month.

items.headline: Unpatched GeoServer zero-day under active exploitation
items.summary: A SQL-injection flaw in GeoServer's PostGIS datastore filter handling (CVSS 9.8) can lead to remote code execution; attackers began probing within hours of public disclosure. Fixed versions — 3.0.1, 2.28.5 and 2.27.6 — are now available.
items.why: GeoServer has a history of being exploited at scale once a flaw goes public — teams running it should patch now.

items.headline: Grok 4.6 rolls out in GitHub Copilot
items.summary: xAI's latest reasoning model is now available across Copilot's Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise tiers, positioned for agentic coding and complex multi-step workflows.
items.why: Widens model choice inside the most widely used coding assistant, days after Grok 4.6's standalone launch.

items.headline: GitHub adds multiple redirect URIs and token refresh for OAuth and GitHub Apps
items.summary: App developers can now register multiple or wildcard redirect URIs and opt into expiring access tokens paired with six-month refresh tokens, replacing indefinitely valid tokens for apps that adopt the new flow.
items.why: Expiring tokens close off a long-standing weak point for any integration whose long-lived token leaks.

items.headline: Cboe files for the first US 3x-leveraged Bitcoin and Ether ETFs
items.summary: Cboe BZX submitted a rule-change application, sponsored by Volatility Shares, for triple-leveraged BTC and ETH products structured as CFTC-regulated commodity pools holding CME/COMEX futures rather than spot assets. The SEC opened the filing for public comment on August 14.
items.why: Would be the most leveraged regulated bitcoin exposure available in the US if approved, though no listing date has been set.

items.headline: Trump expected at White House meeting with crypto CEOs and SEC, CFTC chiefs
items.summary: Trump is expected to attend a session with executives from Coinbase, Ripple, Robinhood, Gemini, Polymarket and Kalshi alongside CFTC chair Michael Selig and SEC chair Paul Atkins, kicking off the CFTC's new Innovation Advisory Committee.
items.why: Sets the stage for possible regulatory movement after the SEC abruptly postponed its Reg Crypto vote and the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate.

items.headline: Binance to block HTX and 10 other platforms over EU Russia sanctions
items.summary: Binance began winding down transaction processing with 16 platforms in a phased schedule, with HTX, EXMO and nine others cut off from August 23 to comply with the EU's Russia sanctions package. It's not a delisting, but transfers to or from the affected platforms trigger a compliance hold.
items.why: HTX is a major exchange; liquidity providers are already pulling back from its books ahead of the cutoff, a sign of the disruption sanctions enforcement can cause even short of a formal delisting.
